- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

contextual_readme_lines.text: **FM1-Lab is our own instrument-first FM sound-design environment.** Its interface and workflow are the product; Felucca's firmware engine is the synthesis foundation, and the upstream emulator remains a supporting compatibility tool.

FM1-Lab runs Felucca's own browser-native WebAssembly firmware inside its AudioWorklet. Felucca owns the audio rendering, voice allocation, FM6 algorithms, envelopes, modulation and effects; FM1-Lab does not substitute a parallel Web Audio FM engine.

Felucca is GPL-3.0-only. Its engine library is MIT and its FM-1 board layer is MPL-2.0. The separate upstream FM-1 emulator is MIT-licensed. Preserve source attribution and corresponding source obligations when distributing builds.

- **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

The FM-1 firmware is bare metal (no vendor SDK) on the open hardware layer of the Felucca family of community firmwares, and installs from a web installer over USB. Until it has been tried on hardware, treat it as experi

| `firmware/fm1/` | The FM-1 side, bare metal: Felucca's hardware layer (`hal/`), start-up and memory map, the update loader (`loader/`), and in `src/`: USB, LCD, storage, the update entry, the panel map, Ravel's platform (`plat_fm1.c`) and the boot, audio interrupt and main loop (`main_fm1.c`) |

`build_fm1.py` builds Felucca's update loader and the app (the platform at `-Os`, the instrument and Beads at `-O2`), checks the image (entry point, no calls from RAM code into flash, no ROM references, no double-precision code, register access only in `hal/`, the RAM and pool budgets) and packages `build/fm1/Ravel-FM1.fwsc`. A release build's identity is `FM-1_82` and the version as two digits each (`0.4.1` is `FM-1_82000401`); a build without a

GPL-3.0 only (see `LICENSE`). The FM-1 platform layer, loader, installer and tools are Felucca's and X0X's (GPL-3.0). The Beads port keeps Mutable Instruments' MIT licence. A firmware package also contains three files of JieLi's AC79 SDK (Apache-2.0). The CZ engine is a port of MAME's uPD933 emulation (BSD-3-Clause). Third-party code is listed in `THIRD_PARTY.md`.

- **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

| `firmware/fm1/` | The FM-1 side, bare metal: Felucca's hardware layer (`hal/`), start-up and memory map, the update loader (`loader/`), and in `src/`: USB, LCD, storage, the update entry, the panel map, Ravel's platform (`plat_fm1.c`) and the boot, audio interrupt and main loop (`main_fm1.c`) |

Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

Felucca began on the FM-1, but it is not intended to stay there. Contributions and ports to other platforms are very welcome. Thirteen engines (6-op FM, VA, phase distortion, chiptune, sampler, granular, physical modelling, organ, drums), four tracks, 64-step sequencer, song mode, mod matrix, USB audio, [web installer](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/), [web editor](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/webapp/editor/) and [browser emulator](https://hu

- [X0X](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) - ReBirth-style groovebox by Charles Vestal: TR-909, TR-808, two TB-303s with TB-3PO acid generators and a breakbeat slicer, each with its own sequencer. contextual_readme_lines.text: Originally developed for a single instrument, Felucca is evolving toward a multi-platform architecture, separating its synthesis engines from hardware-specific implementations. The aim is to make its instruments and sound engines adaptable to different hardware platforms without committing to specific ports or release schedules.
- Related: [Felucca-Engines](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca-Engines) (the ANALOG, LOFI, TRIO, WHEEL, NOISE and PHASE engines, MIT; still maintained) ·

Felucca began on the FM-1, but it is not intended to stay there. Contributions and ports to other platforms are very welcome. If you are interested in bringing Felucca to another device, feel free to open an issue or pull request to discuss it. No specific future ports or release dates are promised.

- **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

contextual_readme_lines.text: ORBIT is a four-track groovebox firmware for the **M-VAVE FM-1**: three synth parts and a drum machine, played through a color-coded Synth / Drum / Event Tape / Mixer workflow. Record a loop, turn it into a song, and keep your favorite sound controls together with user macros. Based on SLOOP/Felucca, with original ORBIT engines and graphics inspired by the original OP-1's four encoder roles.

Thanks to SLOOP's authors and community, and **[Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic) / Hügelton Instruments** for the synthesis, sequencing, editor and update foundations. contextual_readme_lines.text: Originally developed for a single instrument, Felucca is evolving toward a multi-platform architecture, separating its synthesis engines from hardware-specific implementations. The aim is to make its instruments and sound engines adaptable to different hardware platforms without committing to specific ports or release schedules.
- Related: [Felucca-Engines](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca-Engines) (the ANALOG, LOFI, TRIO, WHEEL, NOISE and PHASE engines and the plugin interface, MIT; still maintained) ·
| Browser | Supported | [Try it](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/webapp/try/), no FM-1 needed. |
| Other hardware | Not yet supported | Ports are welcome! Linux-based devices: see the [FAQ](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca/wiki/FAQ). |

Felucca began on the FM-1, but it is not intended to stay there. Contributions and ports to other platforms are very welcome. If you are interested in bringing Felucca to another device, feel free to open an issue or pull request to discuss it. No specific future ports or release dates are promised.

Their synthesizer, DSP, hardware work and tools make this possible. The browser build also follows work from [X0X](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-x0x). - **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

contextual_readme_lines.text: **Status: playable in the emulator; the FM-1 firmware builds, but has not been run on an FM-1 yet.** The whole instrument runs in the browser emulator and the desktop simulator, from the same C sources the firmware is built from. The FM-1 firmware is bare metal (no vendor SDK) on the open hardware layer of the Felucca family of community firmwares, and installs from a web installer over USB. Until it has been tried on hardware, treat it as experi

| `firmware/fm1/` | The FM-1 side, bare metal: Felucca's hardware layer (`hal/`), start-up and memory map, the update loader (`loader/`), and in `src/`: USB, LCD, storage, the update entry, the panel map, Ravel's platform (`plat_fm1.c`) and the boot, audio interrupt and main loop (`main_fm1.c`) |

`build_fm1.py` builds Felucca's update loader and the app (the platform at `-Os`, the instrument and Beads at `-O2`), checks the image (entry point, no calls from RAM code into flash, no ROM references, no double-precision code, register access only in `hal/`, the RAM and pool budgets) and packages `build/fm1/Ravel-FM1.fwsc`. A release build's identity is `FM-1_96` and the version as two digits each (`0.3` is `FM-1_96000300`).

GPL-3.0 only (see `LICENSE`). The FM-1 platform layer, loader, installer and tools are Felucca's and X0X's (GPL-3.0). The Beads port keeps Mutable Instruments' MIT licence. A firmware package also contains three files of JieLi's AC79 SDK (Apache-2.0). The CZ engine is a port of MAME's uPD933 emulation (BSD-3-Clause). Third-party code is listed in `THIRD_PARTY.md`.
- [X0X](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-x0x), a Felucca fork, for the platform as Ravel takes it, the simulator's design, its PNG writer and the build, install and rescue tools.

contextual_readme_lines.text: A source-built Felucca fork for generative ambient music. It adds four-role sound banks (64 recipes), 24 worlds, 24 motifs, 32 scales, seven bounded mutations plus lock, GROW scale variations with exact one-step undo, and six HOME views that edit the actual synthesizer and sequencer state. Full Felucca engine editors remain accessible.

- Felucca-Engines: https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca-Engines commit `c46e0086f69bdc26df1cd144dca9e683cc4531dd`. Its actual source files are vendored in `firmware/firmware/engines/`; no submodule initialization is necessary in this archive.
- Browser emulator design derives through Felucca from Charles Vestal's X0X. Headers and original notices retained.

The output is `firmware/build/felucca.fwsc`. Its internal package identity is Bunker's. **Do not pass `--release`**: that upstream switch overrides the product identity with Felucca's release numbering. One CPU core is the Bunker default. The two-core experiment is not part of this RC2. Keep the original `build.sh` and packaging checks; do not flash `felucca.bin` directly.

The live HTTPS installer in `dist/install/` uses Web MIDI SysEx and user initiation. It verifies package size, SHA-256 and identity before writing. It supports the running FM-1 application and the compatible MIDI OTA loader, checks the final returned identity, and provides AMB-1 1.2 and a locally selected, hash-checked stock V15 package as rollback targets. An intermediate reset to AMB-1 is not required for compatible AMB/Wolf/Felucca update impl

The new installer provides complete Bunker music backup and restore through the existing Felucca archive protocol. Only Bunker RC1/RC2 identities are accepted for music transfers. Explicit consent, complete archive validation and an exclusive tab lock precede restore. This does not export original/AMB projects.

- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

contextual_readme_lines.text: MYCELIUM is a free, open-source alternative firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, built on Felucca and SLOOP. It brings Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, original drum assets and icons, and four factory songs to the hardware.

Based on Felucca by Leo Kuroshita / Hügelton Instruments and SLOOP; upstream copyright notices and asset-specific licences remain in the source archive. Firmware code is GPL-3.0-only; see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and the archive’s `LICENSING.md`. Independent project; no official affiliation with M-VAVE.

- **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

Originally developed for a single instrument, Felucca is evolving toward a multi-platform architecture, separating its synthesis engines from hardware-specific implementations. The aim is to make its instruments and sound engines adaptable to different hardware platforms without committing to specific ports or release schedules.
- Related: [Felucca-Engines](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca-Engines) (the ANALOG, LOFI, TRIO, WHEEL, NOISE and PHASE engines, MIT; still maintained) ·

Felucca began on the FM-1, but it is not intended to stay there. Contributions and ports to other platforms are very welcome. If you are interested in bringing Felucca to another device, feel free to open an issue or pull request to discuss it. No specific future ports or release dates are promised.

contextual_readme_lines.text: - [FM1 Open](https://github.com/m-vave/fm1_open) - M-VAVE's own open firmware repository. V14 adds 8 tracks, 8 sample slots and 16 FX demos; releases carry the development kit, a binary device-engine SDK and a [browser workbench](https://open.m-vave.com/fm1-workbench). Most new firmwares build on it or on fm1-base. GPL-3.0 with the FM1 SDK linking exception.

- [Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca) - Multi-engine synth firmware by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments). Thirteen engines (6-op FM, VA, phase distortion, chiptune, sampler, granular, physical modelling, organ, drums), four tracks, 64-step sequencer, song mode, mod matrix, USB audio, [web installer](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/), [web editor](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/webapp/editor/) and [browser emulator](https://hu

- [SLOOP](https://github.com/isod89/sloop-fm1) - Live four-track groovebox by 3dSam: three synths plus a drum machine, 37 drum kits, punch-in FX, layer system, song mode, web editor. Based on Felucca. GPL-3.0.

- [X0X](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) - ReBirth-style groovebox by Charles Vestal: TR-909, TR-808, two TB-303s with TB-3PO acid generators and a breakbeat slicer, each with its own sequencer. Has a [browser emulator](https://charlesvestal.github.io/fm1-x0x/emu/) and [manual](https://charlesvestal.github.io/fm1-x0x/manual/). Felucca fork. GPL-3.0.

- [BB1 (Big Beat)](https://github.com/TexasRADIO/bb1-firmware) - Rhythm firmware by TexasRADIO: two drum machines (KIT A and KIT B, each with its own pattern) and Dillo, an Open303-derived acid bass, through three-head tape echo and spring reverb. A synthesised 808, and kits that contain samples of the LinnDrum, LM-1, DrumTraks, DMX, Drumulator, Simmons and Rhythm King drum machines; 67 songs and 21 eras at their own tempos, 205 ACID bass phrases

- [GHOULBOX](https://github.com/jasonpersinger/ghoulbox-fm1-dungeon-synth) - Dungeon synth firmware by Jason Persinger: cathedral reverb, worn-tape effect, hurdy-gurdy engine with drones, dark ambient presets and an old-RPG screen. Felucca fork. GPL-3.0.

- [ChoralRoot FM-1](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ChoralRootFM1) - Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords, with voicings, key modes, bass and a looper. [Installer](https://quixotic7.github.io/ChoralRootFM1/) and [browser emulator](https://quixotic7.github.io/ChoralRootFM1/emu/). Built on Felucca. GPL-3.0.

- [Hortator](https://github.com/DeadActive/hortator) - Eight-track drum machine by DEADACTIVE with 808, 909 and Plaits drum models, samples, Mutable Instruments Grids, a pumping compressor and resonators. [Play it in the browser](https://deadactive.github.io/hortator/). Built on Felucca. GPL-3.0.

- **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

- [Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca) - Multi-engine synth firmware by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments). Thirteen engines (6-op FM, VA, phase distortion, chiptune, sampler, granular, physical modelling, organ, drums), four tracks, 64-step sequencer, song mode, mod matrix, USB audio, [web installer](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/), [web editor](https://hugelton.github.io/Felucca/webapp/editor/) and [browser emulator](https://hu

- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).

contextual_readme_lines.text: Originally developed for a single instrument, Felucca is evolving toward a multi-platform architecture, separating its synthesis engines from hardware-specific implementations. The aim is to make its instruments and sound engines adaptable to different hardware platforms without committing to specific ports or release schedules.

| Other hardware | Not yet supported | Ports are welcome! Linux-based devices: see the [FAQ](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca/wiki/FAQ). |

Felucca began on the FM-1, but it is not intended to stay there. Contributions and ports to other platforms are very welcome. If you are interested in bringing Felucca to another device, feel free to open an issue or pull request to discuss it. No specific future ports or release dates are promised.

- **PHYS: physical models.** An eleventh engine, from Felucca 1.0 (the models of DaisySP and Mutable Instruments Rings, by Emilie Gillet): plucked and struck strings, bars and bells, drum heads, and strings with sympathetic strings that ring along. Guitars (NYLON GTR, STEEL GTR, MUTED GTR), PLUCK BASS, KOTO, BANJO, SITAR and TANPURA, PHYS HARP, CHIMES, BIG BELL, VIBRA BAR, STEEL PAN, WOOD BLOCK, CELLO BOW, GLASS BOWL, TABLA, CONGA, TIMPANI and mo
- **NOISE.** A twelfth engine, from Felucca 1.0: noise from analogue to digital, through a resonant filter. WIND, RAIN, OCEAN, VINYL, HISS, RISER, NZ SNARE, BITCRUSH, RADIO, NZ ARCADE, NZ METAL.

| **FM6: six-operator FM, DX7 patches** | A tenth engine: the classic 6-op FM of Dexed (msfa), as Felucca 1.0 ported it — 32 algorithms, a full patch per track, 8 factory patches, a bank of 27 on the FM-1. The web editor edits every operator, **imports DX7 SysEx** (one voice or a 32-voice bank) and stores a whole cartridge in the bank at once. |

A USB keyboard plugged **straight into the FM-1** cannot work: both are USB devices, and a USB link needs a host (a computer, a phone, or a USB MIDI host box). Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP, like Felucca, never switches the radio on.

- **[Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca)** by **Leo Kuroshita** (@kurogedelic) / **Hügelton Instruments** — the engines, the sequencer, the editor, the installer, in 2.3 the USB audio input, the MIDI clock, the knob reading and many fixes, in 2.4 the FM6 engine and its DX7 patch editor (Felucca 1.0 / 1.0.1), and in 2.6 the INSERT effects, LFO 2 (SYNC / TRIG / POL), ENV SYNC, the ANALOG filter types, note LEN and step velocity, MIDI LEAR

- **The Felucca community, who asked for those features first** (Felucca discussions and issues): **Wulgaren** (insert effects with dry / wet, #78; the arp report, #191), **etyrnal** (the lo-fi bit effect, #177; envelopes in note values, #175), **benjaminguerrer** (LFO sync, #154), **gospodindilly-ops** (the ANALOG filter types, #104), **Armstrong1980** (#178) and **oMauNaProducer** (#173) (note length, step velocity), **lostfictions** and **plan
- **renebohne** — in 2.7 MIDI CC 74 sweeps each engine's own cutoff or brightness, after his pull request #71 (Felucca 1.1.5's standard CC map).
